def factor_cycle_phase_duration(df):
    """Long-term trend strength amplified by phase duration, using EMA and ATR."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ema = df_copy["close"].ewm(span=120, adjust=False).mean()
    atr = talib.ATR(df_copy["high"].values, df_copy["low"].values, df_copy["close"].values, timeperiod=20)
    atr = pd.Series(atr, index=df_copy.index)
    distance = (df_copy["close"] - ema) / atr.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    direction = np.sign(distance)
    pos = direction > 0
    neg = direction < 0
    pos_cum = pos.cumsum()
    pos_reset = pos_cum.where(~pos).ffill().fillna(0.0)
    pos_streak = pos_cum - pos_reset
    neg_cum = neg.cumsum()
    neg_reset = neg_cum.where(~neg).ffill().fillna(0.0)
    neg_streak = neg_cum - neg_reset
    streak = np.where(pos, pos_streak, -neg_streak)
    streak = np.sign(streak) * np.log1p(np.abs(streak))
    factor = distance * (1.0 + np.abs(streak))
    factor = factor.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    df_copy["factor_cycle_phase_duration"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_cycle_phase_duration"]
description: Long-term trends and cyclical phase durations: distance from a 120-day EMA normalized by ATR captures trend strength; consecutive days above/below the trend measure phase persistence. Amplifying distance by log phase duration expresses that longer-established trends have stronger cycle-state conviction. This is a Market Structure & Cycle mechanism designed to be informative after industry/size neutralization because it measures idiosyncratic trend phase rather than level.
